claims.claim_text: For each rational prime p, the exponent map from the profinite integers into the away-from-p local unit product is a closed embedding, so the compact quotient B_p is well defined and has a canonical pro-primary decomposition.
Each pro-r factor of B_p has torsion closure P_r and a finite cyclic quotient of order r to the kappa_r(p), with the stated disjoint local formulas for kappa_r(p).
The off-local kernel has finite Ulm invariants aleph_0 and a unique nonzero transfinite invariant at omega plus kappa_r(p) minus one when kappa_r(p) is positive.
The bare compact groups B_p and B_q are topologically isomorphic if and only if kappa_r(p) equals kappa_r(q) for every rational prime r.
The characteristic 11-primary torsion-closure quotients separate B_2 and B_3.
Marked coordinate support, the omitted ambient coordinate, measured structure, flow clocks, traces, operators, and determinants are not invariants supplied by the bare quotient classification.
Injectivity of the full signature p maps to kappa(p), and hence universal recovery of p from B_p, remains open in this work.
The MG11 appendix records bounded declarative conformance fixtures and dependency receipts only; it is not a proof of the classification theorem or evidence of program execution.

manifest_negative_constraints.rule: Do not transfer any theorem about the bare compact group B_p to the actual packet quotient Q_p.
Do not claim that the signature p maps to kappa(p) is injective or that B_p universally recovers p.
Do not claim a flow, periodic-orbit, trace, operator, determinant, Route A, Route B, or Hilbert-Polya result.
Do not describe MG11 declarative receipts as executed computations, formal verification, or global correctness proofs.
Do not claim release, publication, runtime, public-view, or source-execution authority.
